correctness.rationale: The smoothness calculation excludes all gradient-zero points from C; explicit equality G(grad f)=fQ holds over F2 and is checked by the standalone sparse symbolic program. Every G-singularity necessarily has all coordinates nonzero and is one of seven t^7=1 points. Nonzero mixed quadratic term makes each an ordinary node. Bezout plus absence of a line through five nodes proves absolute irreducibility. The Gauss image equals G=0; degree 12/6 gives degree two, and genus-three Riemann–Hurwitz excludes separable degree two. The remaining radicial Frobenius morphism and node-branch correspondence give exactly seven bitangents. Finite arithmetic checks support, but are not substituted for, the geometric proofs.

originality.rationale: A literature-to-claim implication comparison separates the known classical sextic equation and the known characteristic-two seven-bitangent theorem from the presently proved identification of the dual curve with the reduced sextic, its seven exact nodes, and Frobenius normalization. The relevant original sections in Elkies (1998) and Müller–Ritzenthaler (2004) were inspected. The former gives Phi6 and characteristic-two arithmetic without making the geometric dual statement; its Hessian identity contains a denominator 54 not invertible in characteristic two. The latter establishes known equivalence between ordinarity and seven bitangents but not this equation. Pellikaan finite-field incidence material was inspected. Real prior coverage may remain under alternative terminology.
residual_risks: Uninspected nineteenth-century modular projective dual treatments could contain an equivalent equation in different coordinates.
The intrinsic count of seven bitangents is not new; only the explicit classical sextic duality, node geometry and Frobenius factorization are assessed as the new finding.
Publication coverage and independent scientific validation remain incomplete.

value.rationale: The full modular dual geometry of a distinguished smooth genus-three quartic is a natural exact invariant at the exceptional prime. Identification of the reduction of the classical Hessian sextic with the projective dual is non-obvious because the Hessian formula becomes vacuous in characteristic two; the seven exact nodes and Frobenius normalization structurally explain the classical 7-bitangent phenomenon. This is not merely the routine known count or an arbitrary finite subcase.
